rejected.title: Word families for spelling
card: Words that share a root belong to the same family. They share a base meaning and often the same spelling of that base.
Some letters are silent in one word but sound out in a relative. In sign the g is silent. In signal and signature you can hear it.
To spell a tricky word, think of a relative where the hidden letter is clear. Bomb has a silent b, and bombard lets you hear it.
Another example: muscle has a silent c, and muscular lets you hear it. Check that the relative really shares the meaning.
rejected.remember: A relative of a word can show you letters you cannot hear.

a.q: Which relative of the word column helps you remember its silent n?
a.why: Columnar means shaped like a column, and you can clearly hear the n in it. Colony and colour start the same way, but they have a different root and meaning, so they do not help.
a.clue: Look for the word built from column itself.

b.q: Mia is spelling the word autumn and cannot hear the last letter. Which relative shows her that it ends in n?
b.why: Autumnal is made from autumn, and you can hear the n. Autograph, automatic and author begin with similar letters, but they are not part of the same family.
b.clue: Pick the word made by adding an ending to autumn.

a.q: Which pair shows a letter that is silent in one word but heard in its relative?
a.why: The n is silent in condemn but heard in condemnation, and the two share a meaning. Condensation has a clear n too, but it comes from a different root, so it is not a relative. In knee and kneel, and in write and written, the first letter is silent in both words.
a.clue: Say both words in each pair aloud and listen for the same letter.

b.q: Mia is unsure how to spell solemn, because she cannot hear its last letter. Which word would best help her?
b.why: Solemnity is made from solemn and shares its meaning, and you can hear the n in it. Solenoid and insolence also have the letters s, o, l, e and n in a row, but they do not share solemn's meaning, so they are not in its family.
b.clue: A true relative shares the meaning, not just some letters.
